Finbar Dwyer’s

Source: Calua : “bothar gan briseadh” ( down the line )
Trancription : Gian Marco Pietrasanta

A nice jig from a nice album

↳ Posted by gian marco on January 30th, 2003.

It is not the same Finbar Dwyer’s submitted by Will.

↳ Posted by gian marco on January 30th, 2003.

This was recorded by Paddy Reynolds and also by Brian Conway and Tony DeMarco, who called it Paddy Reynolds’ Favorite. Their versions are close and are the basis for this one.

This tune has a few corners in it and I had a time memorizing it.

↳ Posted by edl on May 28th, 2004.

Paddy Reynold’s Dream

I just learned it this winter, great to see this tune again! It took me a while to get hold of the tricky bits too. This was a 1st place winner in the All-Ireland trios some time back. From an old unmarked tape I transcribed the trio setting in addition to the way I learned it. These are both fairly close to the setting you posted (which I think comes from Bill Black), but a few interesting variations.

My favourite bit is the end of the last part in 2 different ways. Overall I love the swing of this jig.

Return to Burton Road

This jig was written by multi instrumentalist, Richard Dwyer. He called it “Return to Burton Road” and recorded it under that name. Larry Egan also told me this, who received it from the composer.

Correct - it’s by Richard Dwyer

Just spoke with Tony DeMarco. It was incorrectly attributed to Paddy Reynolds on an old album of Tony’s. The tune is by Richard Dwyer (confirmed in a conversation between Richard and Tony).
